resale_co.name: Municipal Certificate of Code Compliance (MCC)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of North Plainfield Department of Health, Housing & Property (Property Maintenance / Zoning, Code Compliance Officer)
resale_co.lead_time: Schedule the inspection at least two weeks before closing. The code says the inspection is made within 10 days of the application and fee. Inspections are generally Tuesday and Wednesday 10am to noon and Thursday 1pm to 3pm.
requirements: Inspection for illegal conversions to two-family or multi-family use, illegal rooming units, and living units in basements, attics or other non-habitable spaces
Construction done without permits (sheds, pools, decks, stoves, water heaters, furnaces, additions) must get retroactive permits and inspections; open construction permits must be closed
10-year sealed battery smoke detectors (or the hardwired type required when the home was built) on each floor and within 10 feet of any bedroom
Carbon monoxide detectors within 10 feet of any sleeping area
Handrails on stairs of three or more risers, returned to the wall
Fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)
Vacant house fees paid, taxes and sewer charges addressed, and liens or special charges to the Borough paid
Certificate is issued in the name of the new owner before closing

fees.label: Certificate of Municipal Code Compliance, per dwelling unit (Borough code)
fees.quote: There shall be a fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00) for a Certificate of Municipal Code Compliance per each dwelling unit

resale_co.how_to_apply: Get the MCC application from the Property Maintenance / Zoning page or the Construction/Zoning window at Borough Hall, 263 Somerset Street, and submit it with the fee (exact cash, certified check or money order) at the Property Maintenance window. The inspection is scheduled for the next available date; someone must let the inspector in, and a missed inspection needs a paid reinspection.

evidence.quote: If you are selling your residential property, you must apply for a Municipal Certificate of Compliance (MCC).
The fee for this is $100.00 for single family and an additional $100 for each unit in a multi-family dwelling.

No person shall occupy, permit, or cause to be occupied, any residential premises after title to same has been conveyed, unless a valid Certificate of Municipal Code Compliance has been applied for and issued in the name of the new owner(s) prior to the closing of title.
Inspections should be scheduled at least two (2) weeks before the anticipated closing of the property.
THE MCC WILL NOT BE ISSUED UNTIL ALL OUTSTANDING ISSUES ARE ADDRESSED.

resale_co.notes: Borough Code Section 10-4 (Certificate of Municipal Code Compliance), read on ecode360, bars occupancy after a sale unless the certificate is issued to the new owner before closing. Reinspection fees differ: the application (revised 2/4/2026) says $50.00 per unit, while the code says $100.00 per dwelling unit before each reinspection; the form's three family fee is $300.00. Property Maintenance / Zoning contacts (Borough page): office 908-769-2915; Code Enforcement Officer Kenneth Capobianco 908-769-2913; Property Maintenance Inspectors Tom Allen 908-769-2972 and Michael Garcia 908-769-2329; Secretary Dawn Gaebel, dgaebel@northplainfieldnj.gov. The Rental Certificate of Occupancy ($100.00 per unit), rental insurance and rental registration are rental-only programs.

requirements: Smoke alarms on every level (including the basement) and within 10 feet of bedroom doors; battery units must be 10-year sealed; required type depends on when the home was built (1978-1983 hardwired; 1984-1990 interconnected with battery backup; 1991 on also in each bedroom)
Electric smoke detectors may not be replaced with battery units; defective interconnected detectors must be replaced with compatible units
Carbon monoxide alarm on each sleeping level, in the hallway near each bedroom door
Two family homes: smoke detectors on each landing of common hallways and stairs
Portable fire extinguisher (2A:10B:C, 10 lbs or less) mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen (form still lists it)

authorities.name: Borough of North Plainfield Department of Health, Housing & Property (smoke/CO check is part of the Municipal Certificate of Code Compliance)
authorities.lead_time: Schedule at least two weeks before closing (MCC inspection).
authorities.how_to_apply: There is no separate smoke/CO application for 1-2 family sales. The MCC application doubles as the smoke detector and carbon monoxide certificate application; the housing inspector checks the alarms during the MCC inspection.

evidence.quote: At least one portable fire extinguisher shall be installed in each dwelling unit of the building upon change of occupancy.
He is the Fire Official for North Plainfield, which makes him responsible for all fire inspection related issues in town.
The Fire Official can be reached at 908-769-2934 or by email: fireprevention@northplainfieldnj.gov

LEAID: 1814-001 North Plainfield Fire Prev ... SMOKE DETECTOR COMPLIANCE Name: North Plainfield Boro Housing Addr: 263 Somerset Street ... Enf Auth. Fire Dept ... Fire Official Steven Dill Phone (908) 769-2917 ... Email sdill@northplainfieldnj.gov

fire_cert.notes: The fire code enforcing agency is the North Plainfield Fire Department (Fire Official Deputy Chief Steven Dill, 908-769-2934, fireprevention@northplainfieldnj.gov), but the NJ DCA fire directory lists the smoke detector compliance office for 1-2 family homes as North Plainfield Borough Housing, 263 Somerset Street, (908) 769-2917, and the Borough's MCC application cites the smoke and CO rules. No separate smoke certificate fee is published, so the MCC fee appears to cover it (confirm). The MCC packet still requires a portable fire extinguisher, which state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped from the sale certificate in February 2025.

other_items.label: Vacant house fees, taxes, sewer charges and liens
other_items.detail: Vacant house fees must be paid, taxes and sewer charges addressed, and liens or special charges to the Borough paid before the MCC is issued.

other_items.label: Open permits and work without permits
other_items.detail: Open construction permits must be closed, and work done without permits needs retroactive permits and inspections before the MCC is issued.

other_items.label: Lead inspection (pre-1978 rental homes only)
other_items.detail: If a 1-2 family rental built before 1978 has no record of the required lead inspection, it is required as a condition of the MCC on sale; $120 per unit fee for each lead certificate submitted.

other_items.label: Statement in agreement of sale
other_items.detail: Sellers must include in the agreement of sale a statement on whether any outstanding property maintenance notice or order exists.

open_questions: Does the Borough still require a portable fire extinguisher for the MCC after P.L.2025, c.19?
Is the reinspection fee $50.00 per unit (application) or $100.00 per unit (code)?
Is any separate smoke/CO certificate fee charged, or is it covered by the MCC fee?
How long is the MCC valid?
